title: fix(anthropic): count tool-result documents in document_index citations

files.patch:
@@ -30,6 +30,7 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 * `content_image_url()` with a `data:` URL no longer silently drops the `detail` argument: the setting is now carried by inline image content and forwarded to OpenAI's Responses and Chat Completions APIs (regular image URLs already forwarded it). Other providers continue to ignore `detail`. (#467)
 * `ChatBedrock()` on a Converse model no longer drops redacted reasoning blocks when streaming. They were discarded as they arrived, so a streamed turn lost them, while a non-streamed one kept them. (#468)
 * `ChatBedrockAnthropic()` now uses native structured outputs for `data_model` on Claude 4.5 and later, as `ChatAnthropic()` does. Its Bedrock model IDs (`anthropic.claude-...`, `us.anthropic.claude-...`) weren't recognized, so it fell back to forcing a tool call, which Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 reject with a 400.
+* `ChatAnthropic()` citations backed by `document_index` now count `document` blocks that a tool returns as-is (`ContentToolResult(..., model_format="as_is")`). Before, a citation of such a document, and every citation of a later document, resolved to the wrong source URL or none. (#381)
 * A tool written as a generator (see "Progressive results" in the tool-calling docs) now reports each yielded value in `.chat_async()` and `.stream_async()`, as it does in `.chat()`. A synchronous generator tool used to send the generator object itself (`<generator object ...>`) as its result. An `async def` generator tool now counts as an async tool, so `.chat()` raises the usual "Cannot use async tools in a synchronous chat" error instead of sending `<async_generator object ...>` as the result.
 * MCP tools registered with a `namespace` (in `.register_mcp_tools_http_stream_async()` or `.register_mcp_tools_stdio_async()`) can be called successfully. `Tool.from_mcp()` gains a `name` argument for setting the tool's name independently of the MCP tool's name. (#458)
 * The MCP client used by `.register_mcp_tools_http_stream_async()` and `.register_mcp_tools_stdio_async()` negotiates MCP protocol revision `2026-07-28` with servers that support it. (#456)

+def anthropic_tool_result_document_sources(
+    content: ContentToolResult,
+) -> list[Optional[WebSource]]:
+    """Document slots taken by raw `document` blocks in a tool result.
+
+    A tool can return Anthropic blocks as-is (`model_format="as_is"`), and
+    any `document` block among them is sent inside the `tool_result` and
+    counts toward `document_index`. (`search_result` blocks have their own
+    `search_result_index`, so they don't take a slot.)
+    """
+    # Only an as-is value can carry raw blocks; every other format serializes
+    # to a string. Skip those without rendering them -- this runs for every
+    # citation, and rendering can mean `.to_json()`/`.to_pandas()` calls.
+    if content.model_format != "as_is":
+        return []
+    value = content.get_model_value()
+    if not isinstance(value, list):
+        return []
+    sources: list[Optional[WebSource]] = []
+    for block in value:
+        if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "document":
+            continue
+        source = block.get("source")
+        url = None
+        if isinstance(source, dict) and source.get("type") == "url":
+            url = source.get("url")
+        sources.append(WebSource(url=url) if url else None)
+    return sources
+
+

+def test_anthropic_web_fetch_citation_accounts_for_tool_result_documents():
+    provider = AnthropicProvider(
+        model="claude-sonnet-4-5", api_key="dummy", kwargs=None
+    )
+
+    request = ContentToolRequest(id="call-1", name="lookup", arguments={})
+    prior_turns = [
+        UserTurn("Compare the handbook with https://site.example"),
+        AssistantTurn([request], finish_reason="tool_use"),
+        UserTurn(
+            [
+                ContentToolResult(
+                    value=[
+                        {
+                            "type": "document",
+                            "source": {
+                                "type": "url",
+                                "url": "https://docs.example/handbook.pdf",
+                            },
+                        },
+                        # Search results are cited by `search_result_index`, so
+                        # they don't take a `document_index` slot.
+                        {
+                            "type": "search_result",
+                            "source": "https://kb.example/entry",
+                            "title": "KB entry",
+                            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Entry"}],
+                        },
+                        {
+                            "type": "document",
+                            "source": {
+                                "type": "text",
+                                "media_type": "text/plain",
+                                "data": "Internal notes",
+                            },
+                        },
+                    ],
+                    model_format="as_is",
+                    request=request,
+                ),
+            ]
+        ),
+    ]
+
+    completion = Message(
+        id="msg",
+        type="message",
+        role="assistant",
+        model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
+        content=[
+            web_fetch_result("https://site.example", "Site page"),
+            TextBlock(
+                type="text",
+                text="The handbook, the notes and the site disagree",
+                citations=[
+                    CitationCharLocation(
+                        type="char_location",
+                        cited_text="claim from the handbook",
+                        document_index=0,
+                        document_title=None,
+                        start_char_index=0,
+                        end_char_index=23,
+                    ),
+                    CitationCharLocation(
+                        type="char_location",
+                        cited_text="claim from the notes",
+                        document_index=1,
+                        document_title=None,
+                        start_char_index=24,
+                        end_char_index=44,
+                    ),
+                    CitationCharLocation(
+                        type="char_location",
+                        cited_text="claim from the site",
+                        document_index=2,
+                        document_title="Site page",
+                        start_char_index=45,
+                        end_char_index=64,
+                    ),
+                ],
+            ),
+        ],
+        stop_reason="end_turn",
+        stop_sequence=None,
+        usage=Usage(input_tokens=1, output_tokens=1),
+    )
+
+    turn = provider._as_turn(completion, turns=prior_turns)
+    citations = [c for c in turn.contents if isinstance(c, ContentCitation)]
+
+    assert citations[0].source is not None
+    assert citations[0].source.url == "https://docs.example/handbook.pdf"
+    # A text document has no URL to attribute.
+    assert citations[1].source is None
+    assert citations[2].source is not None
+    assert citations[2].source.url == "https://site.example"
+
+
+def test_anthropic_document_sources_does_not_serialize_tool_results():
+    # Resolving citations walks every prior tool result, but only one sent
+    # as-is can hold document blocks. Serializing other results (e.g. a
+    # DataFrame's `.to_json()`) would be wasted work on every citation.
+    class CountingValue:
+        to_json_calls = 0
+
+        def to_json(self) -> str:
+            self.to_json_calls += 1
+            return "[]"
+
+    request = ContentToolRequest(id="call-1", name="lookup", arguments={})
+    turns = [
+        UserTurn("hi"),
+        AssistantTurn([request], finish_reason="tool_use"),
+        UserTurn([ContentToolResult(value=CountingValue(), request=request)]),
+    ]
+
+    assert anthropic_document_sources(turns, []) == []
+    assert turns[2].contents[0].value.to_json_calls == 0
+
